rationales.1: Each of the three acts carries its own fully-resolved diagram alongside complete qualified copy, plus a consolidated figures section, so the static page reads as a complete illustrated equivalent rather than a stripped fallback.
rationales.2: The value proposition is present in the first viewport, but its more literary sentence structure takes slightly longer to parse than a plainer statement would.
rationales.3: All three flagged figures carry their qualifiers, integrated contextually into each act's own narrative and sidebar rather than clustered only in a footer.
rationales.4: Skip control is present and, notably, rendered as the more visually prominent filled button in the header, making it easy to find without hunting.
rationales.5: Three distinct, well-drafted comparison diagrams sharing one persistent scale reference, plus a considered type pairing, stay coherent across both themes and viewports.
rationales.6: Solid LCP (384/700ms) and frame times (16.9/16.8ms); the same trivial desktop frame-time overage over the 16.7ms budget appears here as in the other candidates.
rationales.7: The door-frame held at one scale across all three acts is an honest, on-message demonstration of the storage claim, though the diagrams read more as scale comparisons than as the boat itself unfolding.
rationales.8: Both declared breaks (water withheld to act three; the human-scale reference persisting throughout) are cleanly and consistently executed with no undeclared breaks visible, and purchase mechanics stay conventional.
rationales.9: Sharp, argumentative copy ('the boat was never the problem. Where to put it was') that could not run on a competitor's page unchanged.
rationales.10: The same instant-static return guarantee applies, but this is the longest of the three pages and a returning visitor depends on the 'Specs and price' anchor rather than a naturally short scroll.
